dedupe_keys.name: climmob online software for tricot agricultural citizen science

description: ClimMob is online software for running tricot (triadic comparisons of technologies) trials, a citizen science method in which many farmers or consumers each compare three options, such as crop varieties, agronomic practices or food products, in their own fields or homes. The platform lets coordinators design large experiments, capture field data offline, monitor progress and data quality, generate automated reports, deliver feedback to farmers, and share projects, datasets and reports between users. It is developed by the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT with MrBot Software Solutions, with funding partners listed on the site. Coverage is global: trials can be organised in any region. Accounts are opened by signing up online; the page read states no price or licence. Caveats: results depend on the design and participants of each trial, and the data sit with each project, not in one public dataset. For simulation it produces on-farm evidence of how varieties perform under real climate conditions, which can parameterise crop and adaptation models and support climate adaptation planning for smallholder agriculture. It is related to the CIAT crop suitability record for Bhutan in this catalogue, another output of the same research centre.
